_comment: Regexes that mark an utterance as too private to send anywhere.
A match REFUSES the turn. Nothing is escalated, nothing is answered, and the
operator is told to handle it himself. This layer cannot route and cannot
send - refusing is the only thing it can do, which is precisely what makes it
safe to trust with the judgement. A layer that could redirect a private
question somewhere else would be making a privacy decision on the operator's
behalf, and a probabilistic privacy decision is worse than none: it makes the
person in front of it relaxed, and relaxed in front of a leaky gate is more
exposure than careful in front of no gate at all.
SHIP NOTHING BY DEFAULT. The list below is an EXAMPLE, drawn from one
operator living in Portugal and running a company there. It is useless to
somebody in Ohio and actively misleading if copied without reading - it will
refuse turns about things they do not have and miss the things they do.
Be trigger-happy when you write your own. A false positive costs one repeated
sentence. A false negative sends the thing you did not want to send.
Matched case-insensitively. Keys starting with an underscore are ignored.
_example_note: Copy to data/sensitive-terms.json and replace with your own.
